direct_prompt: In strategic environments characterized by incomplete information, the ability to deceive opponents through bluffing is essential for maximizing long-term utility. title: A Note on the Inapproximability of Correlation Clustering
human_text: We consider inapproximability of the correlation clustering problem definedas follows: Given a graph $G = (V,E)$ where each edge is labeled either "+"(similar) or "-" (dissimilar), correlation clustering seeks to partition thevertices into clusters so that the number of pairs correctly (resp.incorrectly) classified with respect to the labels is maximized (resp.minimized). The two complementary problems are called MaxAgree and MinDisagree,respectively, and have been studied on complete graphs, where every edge islabeled, and general graphs, where some edge might not have been labeled.Natural edge-weighted versions of both problems have been studied as well. LetS-MaxAgree denote the weighted problem where all weights are taken from set S,we show that S-MaxAgree with weights bounded by $O(|V|^{1/2-\delta})$essentially belongs to the same hardness class in the following sense: if thereis a polynomial time algorithm that approximates S-MaxAgree within a factor of$\lambda = O(\log{|V|})$ with high probability, then for any choice of S',S'-MaxAgree can be approximated in polynomial time within a factor of $(\lambda+ \epsilon)$, where $\epsilon > 0$ can be arbitrarily small, with highprobability. A similar statement also holds for $S-MinDisagree. This resultimplies it is hard (assuming $NP \neq RP$) to approximate unweighted MaxAgreewithin a factor of $80/79-\epsilon$, improving upon a previous known factor of$116/115-\epsilon$ by Charikar et. al. \cite{Chari05}.

human_text: A game-theoretic model is proposed to study the cross-layer problem of jointpower and rate control with quality of service (QoS) constraints inmultiple-access networks. direct_prompt: Asteroid deflection represents a critical component of planetary defense against potentially hazardous near-Earth objects (NEOs). The threat of asteroid impacts has motivated extensive research into mitigation strategies. This review examines the primary methods for deflecting asteroids, the optimal locations for intervention, and the necessary timelines for effective action. Kinetic impactors involve deliberately colliding a spacecraft with an asteroid to alter its trajectory via momentum transfer. NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission successfully demonstrated this technique in 2022 by impacting Dimorphos. Gravity tractors utilize the mutual gravitational attraction between a spacecraft and an asteroid to slowly tug it off course. PCA is employed to reduce the dimensionality of measured vibration data, such as frequency response functions, by projecting the inputs onto a lower-dimensional space that captures the principal modes of variation. title: Collective excitations of hard-core Bosons at half filling on square and  triangular lattices: Development of roton minima and collapse of roton gap
human_text: We study ground state properties and excitation spectra for hard-core Bosonson square and triangular lattices, at half filling, using series expansionmethods. Nearest-neighbor repulsion between the Bosons leads to the developmentof short-range density order at the antiferromagnetic wavevector, andsimultaneously a roton minima in the density excitation spectra. On thesquare-lattice, the model maps on to the well studied XXZ model, and the rotongap collapses to zero precisely at the Heisenberg symmetry point, leading tothe well known spectra for the Heisenberg antiferromagnet. On thetriangular-lattice, the collapse of the roton gap signals the onset of thesupersolid phase. Our results suggest that the transition from the superfluidto the supersolid phase maybe weakly first order. We also find several featuresin the density of states, including two-peaks and a sharp discontinuity, whichmaybe observable in experimental realization of such systems.
direct_prompt: We investigate the collective excitation spectra of hard‑core Bosons at half filling on both square and triangular lattices, with particular emphasis on the emergence and evolution of roton minima. Using a combination of linear spin‑wave theory, numerical exact diagonalization, and series expansion techniques, we map out the dispersion relations as a function of interaction strength and lattice geometry. On the square lattice, we find that increasing nearest‑neighbor repulsion leads to the progressive softening of excitations at specific momenta, resulting in well‑defined roton minima in the dynamic structure factor. For the frustrated triangular lattice, the roton features are more pronounced and appear over a broader region of parameter space, reflecting the enhanced role of quantum fluctuations. We demonstrate that upon approaching critical interaction strengths, the roton gap collapses, signaling an instability toward density‑wave or supersolid ordering depending on the lattice and parameter regime.

title: Photo-z for weak lensing tomography from space: the role of optical and  near-IR photometry
human_text: We study in detail the photometric redshift requirements needed fortomographic weak gravitational lensing in order to measure accurately the DarkEnergy equation of state. In particular, we examine how ground-based photometry(u,g,r,i,z,y) can be complemented by space-based near-infrared (IR) photometry(J,H), e.g. on board the planned DUNE satellite. Using realistic photometricredshift simulations and an artificial neural network photo-z method weevaluate the Figure of Merit for the Dark Energy parameters $(w_0, w_a)$. Weconsider a DUNE-like broad optical filter supplemented with ground-basedmulti-band optical data from surveys like the Dark Energy Survey, Pan-STARRSand LSST. We show that the Dark Energy Figure of Merit would improved by afactor of 1.3 to 1.7 if IR filters are added on board DUNE. Furthermore we showthat with IR data catastrophic photo-z outliers can be removed effectively.There is an interplay between the choice of filters, the magnitude limits andthe removal of outliers. We draw attention to the dependence of the results onthe galaxy formation scenarios encoded into the mock galaxies, e.g the galaxyreddening. For example, deep u band data could be as effective as the IR. Wealso find that about $10^5-10^6$ spectroscopic redshifts are needed forcalibration of the full survey.
direct_prompt: Accurate photometric redshifts (photo-z) are essential for tomographic weak gravitational lensing surveys from space, enabling the division of galaxies into redshift bins to probe the evolution of cosmic structures. This study investigates the photometric redshift requirements for precisely constraining the dark energy equation of state parameters. Ground-based multi-band optical photometry in filters such as u, g, r, i, z, and y provides a baseline for photo-z estimation. Space-based observations complement these with a broad optical filter and near-infrared (near-IR) bands like J and H. Realistic simulations of galaxy catalogs are employed to mimic future space missions and ground-based surveys. An artificial neural network method is used to compute photometric redshifts from the simulated multi-band data. The dark energy figure of merit is evaluated for parameters w₀ and wₐ across various filter combinations and depth scenarios. Adding space-based near-IR photometry significantly reduces photo-z scatter and catastrophic outliers compared to optical-only data. The improvement in the dark energy figure of merit ranges from a factor of 1.3 to 1.7 when near-IR filters are included. Deep u-band observations from the ground can alternatively mitigate outliers by distinguishing reddened galaxies, though near-IR data proves more robust across magnitude limits.
